But my click at (44,44) was exactly the TL W tile of BR's center! And nothing happened. Hmm. So either the click doesn't toggle, or the goal is different.
Wait, maybe the goal is the opposite: the center should have W where the outer has R, and BR's outer is empty so the center should be empty… but clicking the W tile did nothing.
Or maybe the goal is: make BR's outer match its center (add R to the outer ring where the center has W). That is, click the b cells of the outer ring: T? To make outer == center {TL,L,R,BL}, click the outer TL, L, R, BL cells to turn them into R.
Hmm. Which direction? The frame surrounds the whole BR cluster (both outer ring and center).
Or maybe the rule is different: maybe the center should equal the outer of a different cluster (a cross-cluster relationship). Let me check: is BR center {TL,L,R,BL} equal to the outer of any other cluster? TL outer {T,L,B,BR} no; TR {T,L,R,B} no; BL {TL,L,R,BR} no. Close to BL outer but BL outer has BR instead of BL.
Is BR center equal to the center of another cluster? No.
Hmm.
What if the intended complete pattern is: all 4 clusters should be identical? Which target? The frame indicates BR as the "reference"… or the frame indicates the cluster to be changed to match the others. But the other 3 aren't identical to each other either.
OK, another thought: maybe this is a "find the odd one out" quiz: 3 clusters follow the rule center==outer, and BR doesn't. Click the odd one out (the BR cluster) to answer. I clicked the BR center TL tile (44,44) — that's inside the BR cluster — and nothing happened. Maybe I need to click a specific part, e.g., the core (46,46), or the frame itself.
Let me try clicking the BR core (46,46).
Actually wait — I clicked (44,44) earlier and nothing happened. Let me try the BR core (46,46) and the BR outer cells.
Plan: click the BR core (46,46). If nothing happens, click the BR outer TL cell (38,40). If nothing happens, click the frame (34,46).
Let me batch a few single probes with checks in between.

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content:
World model (revised with exact geometry):
- Rule discovered: in TL, TR, BL the center-W pattern exactly equals the outer-R pattern. BR (framed) breaks it: center W={TL,L,R,BL} but outer R=∅.
- The frame likely marks the cluster to fix/answer. My click on BR center tile (44,44) was inert, so maybe the answer is the core or an outer cell.
- Probes: BR core (46,46), then BR outer-TL cell (38,40).
